answer: Every agent identity must be tied to one real place: a grove, a warehouse, any site whose live acoustic echo is recorded fresh each epoch and matched against its registered signature, alongside a photo of a unique pigment marker painted at that spot. A fake identity therefore costs a whole separate physical location — its own echo, its own painted marker, its own recording rig — and renting or faking dozens of distinct sites quickly costs more than the sybil attack can earn.
